alternatives.option: Fence record text verbatim like src/retrieval/render.ts
alternatives.reason_rejected: multi-line fenced bodies blow the 6000-char budget and change every receipt hash; that renderer serves a different packet

alternatives.option: One cap (240) for everything, as the review suggested
alternatives.reason_rejected: truncates ordinary rationales and rulings; 500 for prose keeps them whole in the common case

context: Applied the review of fix/working-set-render (1258c30a): every free-text field now goes through one oneLine() normaliser, hook bookkeeping observations are excluded from the working set, result.error is never rendered, URL userinfo is stripped, 40-hex result shas shortened. 9 new tests, all red on 1258c30a.
rationale: Reviewer showed result.summary, check_method and source_uri interpolated raw so a store-level observation could put '- [RULING (human)] ...' at column 0 of the packet directly above the footer that says class is not changed by wording, and a 5000-char summary pinned the cursor forever. Lane 04's renderer fences bytes verbatim; this renderer is bounded by a 6000-char budget so it must normalise instead — a single line per field is what makes the class label at column 0 the renderer's alone. Two caps because a single 240 cap would truncate ordinary decision rationales (this repo's own store has 300–600 char rationales), while 500 still bounds one decision to ~1 KB. This widens decision 01M2P189MPRZN7K2BP8V2SCHAD's 'bounded to 240' from the key=value path to every field.
summary: Chose one oneLine() normaliser — collapse \s+ to a space, trim, strip URL userinfo, cap with an ellipsis, blank → absent — applied to EVERY free-text field the working-set renderer emits, with two caps: RESULT_RENDER_MAX 240 for observation-derived text and PROSE_RENDER_MAX 500 for ruling statement, decision summary/rationale, post summary and entity name
